title: Tech Note: Introduction to 4D for MySQL and 4D for PostgreSQL

historical_commentary.text: This note introduces two new 2004-era 4D plug-ins, 4D for MySQL and 4D for PostgreSQL, offering a more direct connection path to these popular open-source databases than going through generic ODBC drivers. These specific plug-ins have long since been discontinued as standalone products, and the direct-connector approach they represent has been superseded by 4D's own SQL engine, ODBC/JDBC-based connectivity, and, more recently, ORDA and REST-based integration patterns for interfacing with external open-source databases.
related_updates: The dedicated 4D for MySQL / 4D for PostgreSQL plug-ins are no longer part of current 4D product offerings
4D's native SQL engine (from 4D v11 SQL, ~2007) and general ODBC/JDBC connectivity have become the standard ways to interface with external RDBMSs
ORDA-based data source integration (2018+) offers a more modern entity-based approach to working with external databases
